how.lead: This guide prepares the request. Editing happens on your computer, with your AI and the installed package.
how.step1Title: Say what you want to tell
how.step1Text: Choose the goal, point to the video folder, and set the tone. No timeline skills required.
how.step2Text: The AI checks the environment, works the cut, and prepares an 8–15 second sample. You judge the pace and the look.
how.step3Text: Captions, sound, and motion help tell the story. After your review, the AI finishes and checks the file.

Install.lead: Editing and visual scenes together. A portable skill for Codex and Claude Code, running on your computer.
Install.step1Text: Open your Fassa Frame checkout or package in the folder containing install.py. There is no public fork download yet. Prepare Python 3.9+, uv, FFmpeg/ffprobe, Node.js 22.13+ or 24+, and your AI agent.
Install.step2Text: The installer shares one package between both agents. To use just one, replace both with codex or claude. Restart your agent afterward so it discovers the skill.
Install.step3Text: Run the diagnostic. Resolve missing requirements before rendering.
Install.step4Text: Use $fassa-frame in Codex or /fassa-frame in Claude Code. Ask for a sample before the complete project.
Install.askTitle: Installation starts with a request too.
Install.askRequest: Install Fassa Frame from this repository for Codex and Claude Code using the project installer. Check dependencies with the diagnostic, preserve my settings, and explain what is missing before downloading tools or using paid services.
Install.copyFallback: Copying is unavailable here. The text is selected: press Ctrl+C or ⌘C.
Install.faq1Body: The installer registers one copy at ~/.local/share/fassa-frame, with links at ~/.agents/skills/fassa-frame for Codex and ~/.claude/skills/fassa-frame for Claude Code. Choose one installation method.
Install.faq2Body: Run python3 install.py --target codex or python3 install.py --target claude, then start a new conversation. Registration is local: it does not sync tools or files with cloud sessions or your phone.
Install.faq3Body: Run the installer again. The previous version moves to ~/.local/share/fassa-frame-backups/ and installation .env files are preserved. Keep footage and projects outside the skill folder, and check the update before deleting any backup.
Install.faq4Body: Run python3 install.py --target both --uninstall. Add --dry-run to see the destinations first. Only the agent links are removed; the shared package, settings, backups, videos, and projects stay.
Install.faq5Title: Load as a Claude Code plugin
Install.faq5Body: Run claude --plugin-dir "/path/to/fassa-frame" to load this checkout for one session, then invoke /fassa-frame:fassa-frame. The standalone skill uses /fassa-frame; avoid loading both at once. Video tools and the Python environment are still required.
Install.faq6Title: What runs locally? What costs money?
Install.faq6Body: This guide builds requests and browses examples and scenes. It does not upload or edit footage in the browser. Your agent may require a subscription. Optional external generators may charge fees; the default request asks for your authorization before using them or sending media.
Install.faq7Title: How do I review the first sample?
Install.faq7Body: Listen for clipped words, check caption accuracy, and see whether framing keeps the subject. Ask for changes before finishing everything.
